papers.title: Autocorrelation-based beam shape optimization in scanning electron microscopy
papers.abstract: Many automatically focusing algorithms for scanning electron microscopes exist. Typically, these optimize a single derived metric (such as image sharpness) without considering the intrinsic beam shape. We describe an algorithm to automatically focus and stigmate scanning electron microscopes based on the autocorrelation of captured images. In the first part of this work, we develop the theoretical basis of using the autocorrelation to approximate the current beam shape. In the second part, we use this to condition the beam shape on various surfaces, using Bayesian optimization to tune both working distance and, in particular, stigmation. Through a comparison of the full width at half maximum of the autocorrelation arrays before and after optimization and a visual comparison of images taken of the sample surface before and after optimization, we show that the algorithm is able to successfully optimize the scanning parameters. Overall, our algorithm can effectively focus on a variety of topographies at different magnifications.

papers.title: PlanWAM: Planning-Shaped Future Representations for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: World models in end-to-end autonomous driving predict future scene evolution to provide foresight for trajectory planning. Existing methods mainly study how to predict the future and how to use it, but less often ask which future representation is actually most useful for planning. To this end, we propose PlanWAM, a Planning-Shaped World Action Model. The key idea is to let the planning task shape the future-state representation, so that it retains the information most useful for planning. A latent world model then predicts this planning-shaped future latent representation from historical observations and uses it for planning, enabling foresighted planning. Specifically, we first use a Temporal Register Pyramid to compress multi-frame historical information in a recency-aware manner, learning a compact history representation oriented toward future reasoning and planning. We then introduce a privileged future posterior branch that observes ground-truth future frames, and shape its future latent representation with trajectory-planning objectives to obtain a planning-shaped future latent representation. Hindsight-to-Foresight Distillation trains a prior branch that depends only on history to predict this future latent representation. The predicted future latent representation serves as planning context and guides trajectory generation and selection. PlanWAM achieves 93.8 PDMS / 90.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM-v1/v2 navtest and reaches 38.7 HD-Score on closed-loop HUGSIM in a zero-shot setting, demonstrating leading planning performance across both open-loop and closed-loop evaluations. Extensive experiments further demonstrate that planning-shaped future representations provide an effective and deployable form of foresight for world-action models.

papers.title: CRISP: Fixing Flying Pixels in Latent LiDAR Generation via Diffusion Decoding
papers.abstract: Latent LiDAR pipelines suffer from flying pixels: convolutional VAEs blur sharp radial depth discontinuities, yielding edge depths that back-project to points floating between surfaces. We identify this as a major, directly correctable decoder bottleneck and introduce CRISP: a pixel-space diffusion decoder with a backbone-agnostic latent adapter, DiT-based denoiser, and support mask predictor. CRISP replaces video-VAE and LiDAR-native decoders alike while keeping the encoder and latent generator fixed. Across KITTI-360, SemanticKITTI, and nuScenes, replacing only the decoder reduces FSVD/FPVD by 50.5% on average across frozen backbones; for generic video VAEs, the reductions reach 71%/74%. On the LiDAR-native LiDM backbone, FRID drops by 71%, with the largest gains at depth discontinuities. In a pretrained LiDM world model, the same zero-shot replacement improves FSVD by 15.5%, narrowing the sim-to-real gap.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Generative Conformal Prediction
papers.abstract: Generative conformal prediction builds uncertainty sets from samples of a conditional generator, which are efficient only when the samples represent the response distribution well. This can require many samples, each of which can be costly, as in large diffusion models and scientific simulators, so the sampling budget must be used efficiently. Existing methods draw the same number of samples at every input, wasting samples where the response distribution is simple and undersampling where it is complex, which inflates sets and leaves those inputs under-covered. We propose CASA (Conformal Adaptive Sample Allocation), which characterizes the marginal value of an additional sample and allocates samples across inputs to minimize the expected set size subject to marginal coverage and an average sampling budget. Theoretical analysis shows that adaptive allocation yields smaller sets than a fixed count at the same budget: a missed mode forces a radius that spans the gap between modes, and even oracle radius cannot compensate for it. On synthetic and real tasks, CASA produces substantially smaller sets at the same budget, often improves conditional coverage, and complements existing radius-adaptive methods.

papers.title: How to post-train on a surrogate: Envelope sampling mitigates reward hacking
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are commonly post-trained against LLM judges and other cheap surrogates because the true reward, such as human preference, is too expensive to query at scale. This practice often leads to reward hacking, where reinforcement learning against a miscalibrated surrogate leads to undesirable side effects. In this work, we study a setting in which a small number $n$ of model outputs are annotated with ground-truth labels (e.g., from expert review) and used to recalibrate the LLM judge before optimizing against it. Prior approaches to judge recalibration are costly or heuristic, and it is known that on-policy sampling fails when the surrogate is miscalibrated on a rare set of outputs. In this work, we propose envelope sampling, a theoretically-grounded method for judge recalibration that seeks to minimize an upper bound on the regret of the post-trained model under the assumption that the human reward and re-calibrated reward lie in an $L^2$ ball around the judge. We give practical algorithms to sample from the envelope by rejection or by fine-tuning against a modified reward, and experiments on clinical note generation and on a controlled sycophancy task show that recalibrating on envelope samples mitigates reward hacking where recalibrating on base-model samples does not.

papers.title: BRACE: Differential Privacy for Dense Associative Memory with LSR Energy
papers.abstract: Dense associative memory (DAM) provides an energy-based framework for memory retrieval with close connections to attention mechanisms in modern artificial intelligence. Despite growing interest in differential privacy for AI, the privacy of DAM retrieval dynamics remains relatively unexplored. In this paper, we develop a differential privacy framework for log-sum-ReLU (LSR) dense associative memory, whose finite-support retrieval dynamics pose distinctive challenges for privacy-preserving computation. We propose the Boundary-Responsive Adaptive Correction Evolution (BRACE) algorithm, a differentially private retrieval mechanism for LSR-DAM that adaptively corrects boundary-sensitive perturbations to control their cumulative effect over the retrieval trajectory. In theory, we prove that our method is minimax optimal by deriving dimension-independent terminal and full-trajectory retrieval error rates, with optimal dependence on the inverse temperature and, in the growing-horizon regime, the retrieval horizon. We further establish central limit theorems that enable uncertainty quantification for private retrieval by characterizing its asymptotic distribution and the additional variability introduced by privacy. Numerical experiments compare our proposed method with baseline differential privacy approaches and evaluate its retrieval accuracy. Together, our results provide a theoretical foundation for optimal privacy-preserving retrieval and uncertainty quantification in energy-based associative memory systems.

papers.title: Numerical Neural Operator: Connection Between Numerical Analysis and the Operator Learning and Building Discretized Neural Operators from Finite Element Methods
papers.abstract: Operator learning aims to learn mappings between function spaces and has been widely used for PDE-related problems. This raises two fundamental questions. First, is there a connection between standard numerical methods and neural operators, given that both are designed to approximate PDE solution operators? Second, when a neural operator is trained on numerically generated data, does it approximate the underlying infinite dimension operator, the training data themselves, or the discretized numerical scheme used to generate them? A key hypothesis in the paper is that the trained neural operator may mimic the discretized numerical schemes that generate the training data. The hypothesis has been partially and preliminary verified by the linear approximation principle proposed in Chen Chen 1995 paper and the following scaling law papers. However, neural operator approximation from the perspective of numerical discretization remains unexplored. In this work, we consider a class of PDEs and derive neural operator architectures from the numerical schemes. Firstly, the numerical basis functions, such as finite element basis functions, can be approximated or directly constructed by learnable neural networks. Then the finite difference schemes for temporal discretization can be unrolled into iterative neural architectures that generate the coefficients of the basis of the resulting neural operator. By leveraging numerical analysis, we establish convergence error estimates for these numerically derived neural operators. Notably, the network size depends polynomial on the approximation error in $L_2$, improving the nested exponential dependence derived in the general neural operator approximation and aligning with the numerical observations. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate reduced errors and improved parameter efficiency.

papers.title: FOCUS: From Privileged States to RGB-D with Controlled Modality Switching and Representation Alignment
papers.abstract: Vision-based reinforcement learning for robotic manipulation is sample-inefficient because RGB-D observations are high-dimensional and noisy. Privileged state information available in simulation can accelerate training, but its absence at test time creates a train-test modality gap. We propose FOCUS, a single-stage PPO framework that trains the critic on privileged state while automatically regulating whether the actor collects rollouts from RGB-D or privileged-state latents. Regulation is driven by the KL divergence between the action distributions induced by the two modalities, while representation alignment encourages consistent action selection across them. Together, these mechanisms limit RGB-D rollouts when the actor's action distributions from RGB-D and privileged-state latents disagree. As they align, RGB-D exposure increases, shifting on-policy training toward the RGB-D inputs used at test time. Across five manipulation tasks, FOCUS raises average test success from 0.71 to 0.93 relative to the strongest RGB-D-at-test baseline on each task. When accounting for each method's complete training pipeline, budget-normalized training-success AUC increases from 0.47 to 0.65. On Pick-and-Place, test success rises from 0.47 to 0.86, while AUC increases from 0.12 to 0.61, a 5.0x improvement in learning efficiency over the fixed interaction budget.

papers.title: Cova-PINN: Cross-Domain Conservation Physics-Informed Neural Network for Fluid-Solid Conjugate Heat Transfer in Complex Geometries
papers.abstract: Multi-domain physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) flexibly model medium-specific representations to solve fluid--solid conjugate heat transfer (CHT). However, standard multi-domain PINNs enforce governing equations and interface conditions on separately sampled domain supports, which can yield plausible temperature fields but inaccurate end-to-end energy transfer and outlet temperatures. We propose Cova-PINN, a multi-domain PINN framework that aligns conservation support with thermal interaction paths in complex geometries. Cova-PINN jointly optimizes cross-domain composite control-volume balances at the local scale and paired-wall closure at the global exchanger scale. We evaluate Cova-PINN on four triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) heat exchangers and a geometrically distinct DualMS design against CHT-specific, optimization-oriented, and complex-geometry PINN baselines under a common protocol. Relative to the closest baseline, MUSA-PINN-CHT, Cova-PINN reduces average outlet-temperature and device-level closure errors across the four TPMS topologies by $37.7\%$ and $60.2\%$, respectively, while also improving full-field and heat-duty accuracy, with consistent gains on DualMS.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for predicting homogenized effective properties of one-dimensional composites with imperfect interface
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for materials with enhanced functionalities has driven the development of multiscale methodologies capable of predicting their effective properties from their heterogeneous microstructure and the interfacial interactions. In this work, we develop a coupled multiscale framework combining the two-scale asymptotic homogenization method with physics-informed neural networks to predict the effective behavior of one-dimensional periodic composites with imperfect interface. Physics-informed neural networks solve the local cell problems arising from the asymptotic homogenization method, and the resulting local fields are subsequently used to compute the homogenized coefficients and reconstruct the formal asymptotic approximation. To capture field discontinuities induced by the imperfect interface, a dual-network architecture with suitable optimization strategies is employed. The one-dimensional configuration serves as a reference framework for systematic numerical validation of the asymptotic homogenization method–physics-informed neural networks methodology through direct comparison with the analytical homogenization solution. Numerical experiments consider different interface parameters κ from 1 to 1 0 7 , stiffness contrasts E 1 ∕ E 2 from 1 to 100, with additional calculations up to 1000, and volume fractions V 1 from 0.1 to 0.9. The predicted effective Young’s modulus shows close agreement with the analytical solution, with relative errors ranging from 6 . 21 × 1 0 − 12 to 3 . 55 × 1 0 − 6 , while reconstructed displacement fields for ε = 0 . 01 − 0 . 5 reproduce the analytical solution with root-mean-square errors between 1 . 50 × 1 0 − 11 and 5 . 1 × 1 0 − 7 . Convergence histories show accurate solutions for all tested configurations, while higher stiffness contrasts increase the sensitivity of the physics-informed neural network accuracy to the combined material and interface parameters. These results demonstrate that the proposed methodology provides an accurate computational framework for predicting the effective behavior of one-dimensional composites with an imperfect interface.

papers.title: Crevice Corrosion Mitigation in Ti-6Al-4V DMLS Alloy via Hybrid PEO/PCL/PLA Hierarchical Coatings for Biomedical Implants
papers.abstract: Additively manufactured implants may be vulnerable to localized corrosion within narrow gaps, yet the critical crevice geometry and the effectiveness of multilayer coatings under such conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study compares the crevice-corrosion behavior of direct metal laser sintering (DMLS) and conventionally wrought mill-annealed Ti-6Al-4V alloys and evaluates a hierarchical coating comprising a plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) layer, a polycaprolactone (PCL) seal, and a porous polylactic acid (PLA) breath-figure topcoat. Electrochemical testing was conducted in simulated body fluid (SBF, pH 7.4, 37 °C) using a tapered crevice cell, followed by microscopic, compositional, and topographical analyses. Both uncoated alloys exhibited passive film breakdown; however, the wrought alloy subsequently repassivated, whereas the DMLS alloy underwent sustained localized attack within the critical crevice gap of ~11.4 µm. The transpassive potentials for DMLS and wrought Ti-6Al-4V with PEO/PCL/PLA coating system were 1.32 V and 1.45 V, respectively. Despite the intrinsic porosity and interfacial gaps of the coating, no crevice-type damage was detected in DMLS Ti-6Al-4V. PCL/PLA hierarchy increased the PEO pore resistance to ~3.5 kΩ cm2, reduced the passive current density by ~2 times, and increased the PEO barrier layer resistance to 107 Ω cm2.

papers.title: Hip Arthroscopy in Patients Aged 60 Years or Older Is Associated With Short‐Term Improvement but Variable Arthroplasty Conversion Rates: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To systematically evaluate patient-reported outcomes (PROs), revision rates, and conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA) after hip arthroscopy in patients aged ≥60 years with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome. METHODS: A systematic review of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Scopus was performed in March 2026 in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Included studies reported PROs after hip arthroscopy in patients ≥60 years. Randomized trials, cohort studies, and case series were eligible. Nonoriginal studies, case reports, and studies without PROs were excluded. The largest cohort was selected when overlap existed. Data extracted included patient characteristics, surgical techniques, PROs, and complications, including revision and THA conversion. RESULTS: Seven studies (199 patients, 204 hips) were included. Mean age ranged from 63.2 to 73.0 years, with follow-up from 1.0 to 4.4 years. Among reported cases, 55.6% were Tönnis grade 0, 32.3% grade 1, and 12.1% grade 2. The modified Harris Hip Score and Non-Arthritic Hip Score were most commonly reported, and all studies reported significant postoperative improvements. Revision arthroscopy was infrequent (0%-6%), with an aggregate rate of 2.5% (5/204 cases). THA conversion ranged from 0% to 30%, with an aggregate rate of 11.8% (24/204 cases). Studies with higher conversion rates reported low rates of capsular closure (13%), high rates of labral debridement (up to 77%), low rates of labral repair (20%), and greater prevalence of Tönnis grade ≥1 (up to 57%) and acetabular Outerbridge grade 3 to 4 lesions (up to 44%). CONCLUSIONS: Hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome in patients ≥60 years may provide short-term functional improvement in carefully selected individuals with minimal osteoarthritis and preserved cartilage. However, outcomes are variable, with THA conversion rates from 0% to 30% and substantial heterogeneity across studies. Given short-term follow-up, lack of clinically significant outcome reporting, and variable surgical techniques, conclusions should be interpreted cautiously. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, systematic review of Level III and IV studies.

papers.title: Data-Driven Machine Learning for Uncertainty-Aware Strength Modeling in FDM Additive Manufacturing: A Probabilistic Framework for Reliability-Based Process Optimization of PETG Parts
papers.abstract: Fused deposition modeling (FDM) parts show condition-dependent variability in ultimate tensile strength (UTS), yet most machine learning (ML) studies report only deterministic point estimates, limiting use in safety-critical design. This work presents a probabilistic framework mapping FDM-PETG process parameters to orientation-specific conditional quantile estimates with pooled uncertainty, covering model selection, deployment, and process optimization. A controlled experiment varied 12 parameters across 111 printing conditions from a combined Taguchi and Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) design, yielding 333 ASTM D3039 tensile measurements. Six probabilistic models were trained on raw replicate data and ranked on point accuracy and calibration, weighted 75% toward uncertainty quantification (UQ). The mixture density network (MDN) showed the lowest composite rank. Orientation-specific (MDN-OR) and unified (MDN-UF) variants were compared; MDN-OR gave more conservative lower-quantile estimates for safety-critical design. Lower-quantile (q = 0.05) SHAP analysis identified filament consumption and wall loops as the strongest predictive associations with worst-case strength. For each orientation, the configuration with minimum filament consumption at maximum strength was selected, with its post hoc q = 0.05 lower bound confirmed by physical tensile testing. Within the studied single-material, single-printer setting, the framework shows how probabilistic process–property modeling can support uncertainty-aware parameter selection toward autonomous additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Bridging the gaps in semiconductor digital twins: A structured review
papers.abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is a highly constrained industrial domain, where extreme precision and tightly coupled processes make even minor disruptions critical. Within this domain, digital twins are increasingly recognized as valuable tools for improving system understanding, prediction, and decision support. Despite this potential, current research remains fragmented, with heterogeneous implementations, inconsistent terminology, and uneven technological maturity. Based on a structured screening of 134 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus, this review analyzes 28 peer-reviewed core contributions reporting implemented digital twin or digital shadow solutions in semiconductor manufacturing. We examine the literature by mapping these contributions in terms of operational maturity, architectural intent, technological foundations, and alignment with FAIR principles. The analysis highlights a predominance of system-level implementations, a progressive shift from observability-oriented digital shadows toward more decision-capable digital twins, and a growing adoption of hybrid physics-based/data-driven models, optimization strategies, and AI-enabled control solutions. At the same time, persistent limitations emerge in vertical integration, interoperability, architectural standardization, reproducibility, and data openness. The result is not only a taxonomy of tools and architectures, but also an evidence-based outlook on the future of digital twins in semiconductor manufacturing. This outlook points toward interoperable and reusable infrastructures that bridge simulation and reality, combine human and machine intelligence, and support faster, more efficient, transparent, and collaborative manufacturing.

papers.title: Intelligent Monitoring and Prediction of CNC Tool Wear: Signal Driven, Data Driven and Virtual Real Fusion
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the intelligent monitoring and prediction method of tool wear of computer numerical control (CNC) machine tools, systematically analyzed three representative, technology paths, signal driven, data driven and virtual real fusion. Research shows that the existing methods still have shortcomings in complex working condition adaptability, unsupervised self-label reliability, digital twin real-time performance and cross-process generalization ability. Aiming to these problems, this paper proposes to improve the signal feature extraction, wear state self-identification and visual online detection by combining multi-source sensing information fusion, timing depth clustering, migration learning and digital twin technologies. The research shows that the intelligent tool wear monitoring and prediction needs to be gradually developed from the independent optimization of single technology path to the fusion driving direction of multi-technology collaboration, and the cross-fusion of multidisciplinary methods will definitely become an important direction to promote the transformation to the industrial application with high reliability and strong generalization ability.

papers.title: PDE-constrained structural correction: A physics-informed mechanism for mismatched ODEs in coupled systems
papers.abstract: Coupled partial differential equation–ordinary differential equation (PDE–ODE) systems arise in many physical, biological, and engineering applications, where parameter mismatches in the ODE subsystem can substantially degrade state reconstruction. This work investigates whether accurate PDE constraints can structurally correct mismatched ODE dynamics during joint optimization. We develop a PDE-constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework with a multi-component loss that enables systematic control of the relative influence of PDE and ODE constraints. Theoretical analysis shows that minimization of the PDE residual can provide a global regularization effect through the coupling between the PDE and ODE states. Numerical experiments and ablation studies further demonstrate that dense PDE constraints generate a strong optimization signal that can counteract the influence of a mismatched ODE model and guide the inferred ODE trajectory toward the ground truth. For the three tested parameter offsets ( 𝛿 ⁢ 𝜇 = 0 . 1 –0.3, corresponding to relative deviations of 12.5%–37.5%), the proposed framework reduces the state reconstruction error by an average of 48.6% compared with direct integration of the mismatched ODE. These results indicate that partially accurate physical knowledge can compensate for model mismatch in coupled systems and provide a useful perspective for inverse problems and system identification.

papers.title: Assessment of uncertainty estimation and distillation for reliable 3D dental mesh segmentation in orthodontics
papers.abstract: Abstract The integration of deep learning into computer-aided orthodontic treatment planning has enabled automated tasks such as tooth segmentation from 3D dental models. However, the reliability of these systems remains a concern due to their black-box nature and tendency toward overconfident predictions. In this work, we present a comprehensive evaluation of uncertainty estimation methods for tooth segmentation on 3D intraoral scans. We investigate several state-of-the-art neural network architectures combined with uncertainty estimation techniques including predictive entropy, Monte Carlo dropout, test-time augmentation, deep ensembles, and evidential deep learning. Evaluation on the Teeth3DS benchmark, supplemented with synthetically incomplete scans and a custom out-of-distribution dataset, shows that sampling-based approaches, particularly deep ensembles, provide the most reliable uncertainty estimates. In contrast, entropy-based methods and evidential deep learning often produce overconfident predictions and fail to identify major segmentation errors. We further demonstrate that uncertainty estimation can detect out-of-distribution samples such as scans with artifacts or missing regions. Although deep ensembles provide the most reliable uncertainty estimates, their computational cost limits practical deployment. We therefore investigate uncertainty distillation and show that a single student model can achieve ensemble-like uncertainty quality with only one forward pass.

papers.title: DREAM: Defensive risk-aware enhanced maneuver planning for autonomous vehicles in heterogeneous traffic
papers.abstract: Autonomous highway overtaking and merging remain hazardous when a large vehicle masks a fast-approaching agent until its path intersects the ego maneuver. Reacting only after line-of-sight recovery leaves little braking margin, whereas uniform caution produces disruptive deceleration toward shadows that are in fact empty. Existing risk-field planners largely score a static or externally supplied map and couple it to one planning layer, which precludes coordinated pre-reveal intervention. We introduce DREAM, which treats occlusion-conditioned latent hazard as a transported physical state governed by an inertial advection–diffusion–reaction partial differential equation, and injects the resulting Cartesian field into Frenet-domain model predictive control with control barrier functions through maneuver-level decision veto, risk-adaptive barrier modulation, and horizon-wise cost shaping. Evaluation spans controlled Python episodes, paired trailer-occlusion ablations, sensor-mediated CARLA experiments, naturalistic Bird-eye-view dataset trajectories replay, and a ROS 2 platform demonstration. The propagated field withdrew the requested merge about one second before the hidden actor became planner-visible, raised minimum hidden-actor clearance by 0.428 m, and lowered collision-or-near incidence from 29/30 to 19/30 in dense traffic, at a bounded empty-shadow speed cost. Under inD replay it tracked logged human speed profiles more closely than non-field and reduced-field variants, indicating calibrated anticipation rather than uniform conservatism. This evidence supports improved anticipatory hidden-interaction margins. The code implementation and selected scenario demonstrations for this study could be found at https://github.com/SAS-HKU/DREAM.git .

papers.title: Multi-setup Bayesian FFT modal identification with multiple modes leveraging on second order information
papers.abstract: Conventional multi-setup Bayesian operational modal analysis (OMA) algorithms may suffer from low efficiency and false convergence when dealing with closely-spaced modes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Newton-type Bayesian FFT algorithm to minimize the negative log-likelihood function (NLLF). The gradient vector and Hessian matrix, i.e., the first- and second-order derivatives of NLLF with respect to modal parameters, are obtained semi-analytically by exploring a latent variable structure of NLLF through the expectation–maximization (EM) formulation. The sparsity of the Hessian matrix is explored to enable a fast and robust implementation. In the optimization, an existing EM algorithm is employed in the first round of iterations to improve the positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian matrix, and Newton iterations are then performed to refine the estimate. Since the inverse of Hessian matrix is available at each iteration, the posterior covariance matrix is obtained as a by-product under the Laplace approximation, providing uncertainty quantification without additional computation. A synthetic example of a 30-story shear-type building and a field test of the 292 m SEG Plaza are applied to illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm. Results show that the proposed algorithm achieves high accuracy and fast convergence, while the existing method may fail in challenging scenarios, e.g., multiple closely-spaced modes.

papers.title: Data-driven asynchronous optimal control for 2-D MJRSs with structural constraints via reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: This article investigates the data-driven asynchronous structured optimal control problem for discrete-time two-dimensional (2-D) Markov jump Roesser systems (MJRSs) with unknown dynamics. The structural coupling of 2-D systems motivates a structured optimal control formulation. Moreover, the proposed framework addresses the challenges associated with asynchronous mode information and unknown system dynamics. To resolve these issues, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework is established to solve the derived asynchronous discrete-time algebraic Riccati equation (ADARE) using only measurable input-state data. Two data-driven algorithms are developed to achieve this objective. First, an off-policy policy iteration (PI) algorithm is constructed to reconstruct the optimal controller. Second, a value iteration (VI) algorithm is proposed to circumvent the requirement of an initial stabilizing policy inherent in the PI algorithm. Crucially, the VI approach facilitates online learning from arbitrary initial conditions. Theoretical analyses guarantee the convergence of both algorithms to the structured optimal solution and ensure the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework under asynchronous conditions.

papers.title: Deployment-time action correction for steady-state reinforcement learning-based optimal power flow
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of constraint violations in reinforcement learning (RL) for power-system operation, with application to steady-state optimal-power-flow tasks. While RL-based controllers can achieve competitive reward performance, they may produce actions that violate operational constraints, limiting their practical applicability in steady-state optimal-power-flow (OPF) tasks. We investigate a deployment-time safety framework in which a continuous constraint-violation surrogate is learned directly from state–action–violation samples generated by the power-system simulator. Once the nominal Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) policy has been trained, it remains fixed, and candidate actions are corrected by minimizing their deviation from the original policy output while penalizing the violation predicted by the learned surrogate. The correction is performed directly over the nonlinear surrogate using projected gradient descent, and linear and quadratic penalty formulations are empirically compared. The framework is evaluated on two complementary OPF-Gym benchmarks, EcoDispatch and MaxRenewables, which differ in their optimization objectives, network topologies, actuator compositions, and control dimensionalities. Large-scale out-of-sample simulations show substantial reductions in the frequency and severity of constraint violations relative to nominal SAC, Lagrangian-penalty SAC, Recovery RL, and linearized correction baselines; across both benchmarks, the exact-gradient variants substantially reduce physical constraint violations relative to nominal SAC and the linearized correction strategies. In EcoDispatch, these feasibility improvements are additionally achieved while maintaining reward performance close to the underlying SAC controller. The results demonstrate the potential of simulator-driven deployment-time action correction for improving the empirical feasibility of RL-based OPF decisions without retraining the nominal policy or requiring the analytical OPF constraints to be exposed in differentiable form.

papers.title: Physics-informed digital twin for optimal operation of solar air source heat pump-based district heating systems
papers.abstract: District heating systems (DHS) are increasingly required to support low-carbon building energy supply; however, conventional fossil-fuel-based DHS suffer from high energy consumption, thermal losses and limited flexibility under variable solar availability and heating demand. Solar air-source heat pump systems improve renewable heat utilization, but their practical operation is challenged by intermittent solar irradiance, nonlinear coupling among the solar collector, heat pump, thermal storage and load-side distribution loop and the need for accurate real-time state estimation and control. Existing rule-based and proportional–integral–derivative (PID) strategies lack predictive capability, while conventional model predictive control (MPC) and digital-twin approaches often rely on simplified linear or quasi-static models that cannot fully capture heat-pump nonlinearities, model uncertainty and thermodynamic constraints. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a physics-informed digital-twin district heating system (PI-DT-DHS) based on a physics-informed neural network (PINN) for a solar air-source heat pump. The proposed framework models the solar air heater, evaporator, condenser, thermal storage tank and load-side loop using coupled thermodynamic energy-balance equations, while the PINN embeds supervised reference-data fitting, physics residuals, boundary conditions, energy conservation and operational constraints into the learning process. The trained digital twin is further combined with a constrained optimization layer to minimize compressor power, auxiliary heating, load-temperature deviation and storage-temperature fluctuation under operational limits. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PI-DT-DHS reduces compressor energy to 19.7 kWh , auxiliary heating to 8.9 kWh , storage loss to 2.4 kWh and distribution loss to 2.0 kWh , while increasing useful heat delivery to 39.5 kWh compared with other district heating configurations.

papers.title: Clinically benchmarked and interpretable machine learning for preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian tumors
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a highly fatal gynecological malignancy, largely because it is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage. Although machine learning (ML) has shown promise for ovarian cancer classification using clinical laboratory data, many existing models operate as black boxes, limiting clinical interpretability. This study proposes an interpretability-centered ML framework for distinguishing malignant from benign ovarian tumors using a publicly available, retrospective, single-center Chinese cohort from the Third Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, comprising 349 patients with 171 malignant and 178 benign ovarian tumors. Variables with excessive missingness were excluded, while retained missing values were mean-imputed and features were min–max normalized. Imputation statistics and normalization parameters were estimated exclusively from the training data and applied unchanged to the evaluation data to prevent information leakage. Five classifiers, support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbor, discriminant analysis, decision tree, and logistic regression, were evaluated using Bayesian hyperparameter optimization. SVM achieved the highest accuracy of 93.7% and sensitivity of 95.3% considering the leave-one-out cross-validation. The proposed framework optimizes both predictive and explanation stages: Bayesian optimization first tunes the classifiers, followed by joint optimization of LIME perturbation sample size and kernel width. The optimized LIME surrogate achieved 91.9% accuracy, only 1.8% points below the SVM, while identifying CA125 and CA19-9 as the dominant positive predictors of malignancy, consistent with established clinical knowledge. These findings indicate that systematic calibration can improve the fidelity and stability of patient-level explanations, although stronger predictive results have been reported on the same dataset and external validation remains necessary. However, prospective, multicenter, and clinician-in-the-loop validation is required before clinical decision-support use.

papers.title: A fast risk assessment method for power balance under extreme weather conditions based on deep reinforcement learning with a coupled attention mechanism
papers.abstract: Even if persistent stagnant weather does not directly damage power grid equipment, it may lead to prolonged insufficient output of renewable energy sources and further trigger power balance risks. This paper proposes a rapid risk assessment framework that comprehensively incorporates meteorological sensitivity models, time-varying component failure probabilities, a Denoising Variational Autoencoder (DVAE) for generating coupled wind-photovoltaic-temperature scenarios, and a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) model embedded with the feature token attention mechanism.The 72-hour assessment task is formulated as an offline Markov Decision Process (MDP): the state space covers meteorological conditions, power sources, power grid topology, load profiles, and risk features of the previous time step; continuous actions are defined as risk indicator vectors; the reward function is designed to penalize deviations between model outputs and PSD-BPA benchmarks, temporal inconsistency, and violations of physical constraints.To distinguish the sequential reinforcement learning formulation from direct regression, a feedforward Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) is introduced as the non-reinforcement learning baseline. Four metrics, namely Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R2), and the 95th percentile of absolute error (P95AE), are adopted to evaluate all models on an independent scenario-level test set.Verified on the planned power grid of Northeast China in 2025 as the test case, the proposed DDPG-Attention achieves MAE of 0.0310, RMSE of 0.0389, R2 of 0.954 and P95AE of 0.0760 on the independent test set. The average time consumption for a single risk assessment is approximately 0.12 seconds, yielding an acceleration ratio of multiple orders of magnitude compared with the traditional time-sequential Monte Carlo simulation based on PSD-BPA. This study provides an efficient and accurate novel technical paradigm for the rapid evaluation of power supply-demand imbalance risks in power systems under extreme weather conditions.

papers.title: Smart-water enhanced oil recovery in carbonate reservoirs: experimental validation, 3D numerical modeling, and optimization
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs exhibit complex flow behavior, strong wettability variations, and early water breakthrough, which limit the efficiency of conventional water flooding and reduce oil recovery. Smart-water injection has emerged as a promising enhanced oil recovery (EOR) technique; however, its field-scale application remains challenging due to uncertainties associated with ion composition, reservoir heterogeneity, and injection strategies. This study develops an integrated multi-scale workflow that combines smart-water laboratory experiments, core-scale validation, 3D reservoir simulation, uncertainty quantification, and optimization to evaluate and maximize smart-water performance in the WQ1-57 carbonate reservoir. Experimental investigations demonstrate that engineered brines enriched with optimized concentrations of sulfate (SO₄ 2 ⁻), calcium (Ca 2 ⁺), and magnesium (Mg 2 ⁺) ions promote wettability alteration toward more water-wet conditions, resulting in incremental oil recovery of 11.7–22.8% at core scale. A calibrated numerical model was developed using the MATLAB Reservoir Simulation Toolbox (MRST) and validated through history matching before being upscaled to reservoir scale. Simulation results reveal that smart-water injection can achieve up to 18.0% incremental oil recovery, delay water breakthrough by 0.1–0.3 pore volume (PV), and improve areal and vertical sweep efficiencies by up to 14% and 20%, respectively. Sensitivity analysis identifies horizontal permeability, sulfate concentration, and injection pattern as the dominant controlling parameters, contributing up to 18%, 12%, and 14% variations in recovery performance. Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis confirms the robustness of the proposed approach, with predicted recovery factors ranging from 32.8% to 55.3% (mean value: 46.4%) and incremental recovery ranging from 6.1% to 12.8% under P90-P10 uncertainty scenarios. The optimization framework further identifies that horizontal production wells combined with layered conformance-controlled smart-water injection provide the optimum development strategy, achieving a maximum incremental recovery of 18.1%. The novelty of this work lies in integrating experimental ion optimization, uncertainty-aware reservoir simulation, and intelligent injection optimization within a single workflow, providing a scalable methodology for designing robust smart-water EOR strategies in heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs.

papers.title: Climate-adaptive amine sweetening optimization via the critical reversal temperature for seasonal mercaptan-accumulation and dehydration control
papers.abstract: Seasonal temperature variability can fundamentally alter the limiting mechanism in industrial amine gas sweetening, creating a trade-off between low-temperature methyl-mercaptan accumulation and high-temperature dehydration demand that cannot be adequately addressed by a single annual operating point. Here, we develop a climate-adaptive, cost-aware optimization framework for an industrial methyl diethanolamine-piperazine (MDEA-PZ) sweetening system exposed to ambient temperatures from -4 to 46°C. A calibrated reduced-order model was constructed from eleven plant-validated seasonal operating states and evaluated using leave-one-season-out (LOSO) validation, yielding mean absolute percentage errors of 0.040% for reboiler duty, 2.34% for methyl mercaptan concentration, and 9.46% for sweet-gas water content. A polynomial Ridge surrogate trained over a 1400-point Latin hypercube design subsequently achieved a mean R² of 0.9782, a minimum R² of 0.9381 across all outputs, and a maximum MAPE of 2.05%. The central contribution is the identification of a Critical Reversal Temperature (CRT), defined here as the ambient temperature at which the dominant normalized operating burden switches from a methyl-mercaptan accumulation proxy to sweet-gas dehydration; it is not presented as a direct corrosion-rate threshold. For the nominal benchmark composition and solvent strength, the CRT was 19.61°C, and water-content, normalization-bound, and TOPSIS-weight sensitivity tests consistently retained the thermal-policy transition near 20°C. In contrast, exploratory off-design composition/solvent-strength scenarios shifted the modeled CRT over a wider 8.36-24.22°C range and are explicitly treated as scenario exploration rather than independently plant-validated predictions. Relative to the reference seasonal operation, the model-based CRT-adaptive screening strategy reduced annual OPEX from approximately 11.5 to 9.8 MUSD yr⁻¹, corresponding to about 1.8 MUSD yr⁻¹ in annual savings; the 15-year incremental NPV was approximately 16.2 MUSD with a simple payback of about 0.5 years. Because off-design circulation response is semi-empirical, the adaptive setpoints and associated economic outputs should be interpreted as screening predictions pending high-fidelity or plant re-validation. These results establish CRT as a physically interpretable regime-transition descriptor conditional on the benchmark model and provide a control-oriented framework for climate-responsive operation.

papers.title: An integrated framework for explainable and uncertainty-aware software defect prediction with adaptive risk scoring and multi-task deep residual learning
papers.abstract: Software defect prediction (SDP) is a challenging problem in SQA, the majority of the approaches that have been proposed so far focus on this problem as a binary classification problem, without taking into account the risk associated with each defective module. This paper introduces an integrated framework of adaptive risk scoring, Multi-Task deep residual learning with gated feature attention, Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification, and SHAP-based explainability that is applied simultaneously towards both defect detection and risk classification. This is due to a data-d Single-Task riven parameter λ optimized via a Spearman correlation used to calculate the risk score and SMOTETomek resampling and focal loss to address severe class imbalance. A defect detection ROC-AUC of 0.9581, F1-score of 0.5928, and recall of 0.7616 is achieved by the proposed model on the pc5 dataset; while a macro F1-score of 0.98 and accuracy of 0.99 are achieved by the proposed model on the risk classification task, in which the three risk classes are model-derived prioritisation tiers rather than independently validated defect-severity labels. Monte Carlo Dropout also identifies 25.2% of modules as high uncertainty candidates for manual review, while feature attribution shows that cyclomatic density, comment percentage and global data density are the most important features affecting defect risk.

papers.title: Hierarchical coordinated control strategy based on temperature-pressure path separation for CSP plants using CO2-based mixtures
papers.abstract: Coupling a CO 2 -mixture Brayton cycle with parabolic-trough collectors offers considerable potential for improving the efficiency and load-regulation flexibility of concentrated solar power plants. However, over a wide operating range, the strongly nonlinear and coupled thermophysical properties of the fluid create multivariable control challenges that conventional PI control cannot adequately address. Accordingly, this study develops a three-mode hierarchical coordinated control strategy based on temperature–pressure pathway separation and integrates it with nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) using a ‘physics-based backbone + neural network’ prediction model. Full-range optimized operation is achieved through mode partitioning and coordinated controller action, while the physical origins of performance differences among modes are interpreted from the response of working-fluid properties. Compared with linear model predictive control, NMPC reduces the integral absolute error of strongly coupled variables by 35.5%-67.4% and lowers the mean relative error of all variables by 39.2%-53.5% under sustained noise disturbances. Under representative daily conditions, Mode 1 reduces the standard deviations of density and specific heat capacity on the winter solstice by 81.8% and 82.5%, respectively, relative to Mode 2, thereby suppressing thermophysical-property fluctuations and providing more stable operating conditions for NMPC. This provides more stable conditions for NMPC, which limits the regulation time of key variables to approximately 300 s. Across four representative days, the maximum mean absolute errors of turbine inlet pressure and net power output are 72.76 kPa and 231.51 kW, respectively. The proposed framework offers an effective solution for wide-load operation and coordinated multivariable control of strongly nonlinear mixed-fluid solar thermal systems.

papers.title: Research progress on the application of multi-cup reconstruction techniques in hip revision surgery for severe acetabular defects
papers.abstract: With the increasing number of primary total hip replacements, severe acetabular defects have become a major challenge in revision total hip replacement, particularly Paprosky Type IIC–IIIB defects. Traditional reconstruction methods still have certain limitations in terms of initial stability, bone preservation, and long-term fixation. In recent years, multi-cup reconstruction techniques using modular porous metal acetabular components have been increasingly explored as an alternative approach for the reconstruction of complex acetabular defects. This review aims to summarize research progress on multi-cup reconstruction techniques and examine their clinical applications, potential mechanisms, and future directions. This narrative review summarizes recent basic biomechanical research and clinical studies focusing on multi-cup reconstruction techniques, including their biomechanical and biological mechanisms, classification of assembly configurations, intraoperative implantation strategies, clinical indications, postoperative functional outcomes, complications, and reported outcomes relative to other acetabular reconstruction methods. Available evidence suggests that multi-cup reconstruction may increase host bone–implant contact, facilitate restoration of the hip center of rotation, and provide a mechanical environment potentially favorable for load transfer and biological fixation. Published clinical studies have reported generally favorable short- to mid-term functional and radiographic outcomes after multi-cup reconstruction. However, the existing evidence is predominantly derived from single-center retrospective case series and other low-level observational studies; high-quality prospective comparative studies and long-term follow-up data remain limited. Therefore, the optimal selection of prosthesis configurations, the long-term durability of the constructs, and their role in patients with pelvic discontinuity remain uncertain. Overall, multi-cup reconstruction represents a technically feasible option that may be considered for selected patients with severe Paprosky Type IIC–IIIB acetabular defects when adequate residual host bone and initial fixation can be achieved. Its potential biomechanical and biological advantages remain incompletely established, and further multicenter prospective comparative studies with long-term follow-up are needed to determine its clinical effectiveness and appropriate indications. Future research may also evaluate the potential contribution of digital preoperative planning, AI-assisted decision-making, and patient-specific implants to the individualized application of multi-cup reconstruction.

papers.title: An innovative approach of project-based learning applied to the teaching of biochemistry
papers.abstract: Most of the research in biochemistry education describes approaches that include teaching with constructivist ideas, since the approach with lectures has been criticized for promoting superficial learning. Thus, biochemistry learning should not only achieve proficiency of knowledge but also critical thinking skills and the interconnection of knowledges. Although Case-Based Learning is the most frequent methodology, Project-Based Active Learning, using individual and collective strengths, has received attention in recent years. With the aim of encouraging learning through doing, experimenting, problem-solving, teamwork, developing social skills, understanding, collaboration, partnership, and responsibility, the activity "Projeto de Divulgação Científica" has been implemented in the Integrated Biochemistry course of different undergraduate programs at Universidade Federal de São Paulo, since the pandemic. The students divide themselves into groups and the development of skills such as selection of bibliography, collaboration, communication, contextualization are their responsibility since the students are free to choose the project theme and conduct. In 2023 the overall failure rate in the course was 10% lower when compared to 2018 rates, before the project’s implementation. Additionally, a shift was observed over the years in the diversity of presentation formats. Initially, 28 out of 50 presentations were in pamphlet form. Recently, there has been a significant increase in the use of Instagram and videos, including TikTok, probably due to this generation's greater interest in social media. It can be concluded that both active student participation in the Projeto de Divulgação Científica activity and the increase in the number of extensionist students in the Instagram Project reflect the acceptance of this activity by undergraduate students as a form of learning and scientific literacy development. Furthermore, this approach has increased students' interest in biochemistry and scientific outreach, as indicated by the growing number of followers of the Scientific Outreach page (@bioquimatch_unifesp). This methodology has contributed to more effectively integrating students into the discipline and covering all topics discussed throughout the semester, thereby fostering increased interest among both students and the general population in science.

papers.title: Performance Assessment of Sensorless Controlled Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors for Electric Vehicles Under Realistic Drive Cycles
papers.abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are widely employed in electric vehicles (EVs) owing to their high efficiency, high power density, and reliability. Although sensors may raise costs, the accurate estimation of both rotor position and actual speed is crucial to achieve high motor performance. This paper presents a comparative assessment of sensorless PMSM drive control using field-oriented control (FOC) and model predictive control (MPC) under various representative automotive drive cycle conditions. A model reference adaptive system (MRAS) observer is employed to estimate rotor position and speed, and the complete drive system is simulated via MATLAB/Simulink R2025b. Performance is assessed using representative synthetic urban and highway drive cycle segments, designed to capture key dynamic features (stop-and-go transients, steady-state cruising, and road grade variation) analogous to those found in standardized cycles such as WLTP, considering speed tracking error, torque ripple, and current/estimation quality indicators. The results indicate that FOC–MRAS provides robust steady-state behavior and reliable estimation under low-speed urban segments, whereas MPC–MRAS achieves faster transient response and improved current regulation in higher-speed segments at the expense of increased computational complexity. The reported findings elucidate the practical trade-offs between robustness and predictive capability and provide simulation-based guidance for selecting sensorless control strategies for PMSM-based EV traction drives.

papers.title: A review of remote sensing for agricultural drought: technologies, indices, modelling advances and future prospects
papers.abstract: Agricultural drought is a complex hazard that jeopardises food security and progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed English-language literature published between 2015 and 2025, focusing on Remote Sensing (RS)-driven agricultural drought monitoring and prediction. Eligible studies were identified from the Web of Science and Scopus databases (last searched in August 2025); review articles, duplicates, and irrelevant studies were excluded, resulting in 181 articles. This review critically examined the evolution of sensors, drought indices, modelling approaches, and emerging technologies used to assess agricultural drought across diverse agro-ecological regions. Specifically, we (1) systematically evaluated the use of optical, thermal, and microwave RS platforms, along with satellite-based, model-based, and reanalysis products for agricultural drought monitoring; (2) reviewed widely used RS-based drought indices, including single indices grouped into nine categories, as well as composite indices; (3) reviewed software or programming languages applied; (4) assessed the progression of modelling approaches from traditional statistical and time-series methods to machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) frameworks; and (5) examined validation strategies applied to agricultural drought assessment. The analysis reveals a growing research interest in this topic, with a strong geographic concentration in Asia, particularly China. Optical and thermal platforms (e.g. MODIS and Landsat) dominate the literature (~54%) due to their accessibility, followed by satellite-derived precipitation products (17%), while microwave soil-moisture missions remain underutilized (~7%). Regarding RS-based indices, most studies employed more than one index: 44% analysed multiple individual indices, 51% used composite indices (either alone or in combination with individual indices), and only 5% relied on a single index. Vegetation indices, such as NDVI, remain workhorses; however, their sensitivity to soil background effects and canopy saturation has driven increased adoption of thermal composites (e.g. VHI), as well as adaptive weighting schemes and principal component analysis-based approaches. Moreover, computational tools used in drought research can be broadly grouped into geospatial and RS platforms for large-scale data processing and analysis (e.g. QGIS, GEE), and general-purpose programming languages (e.g. R, Python) for model development and advanced analytics. Regarding the methodology, statistical and time-series approaches account for 64% of the reviewed studies, followed by ML models (20%) and DL methods (15%), while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) remains nascent. Techniques, such as random forests, support vector machines, and CNN and LSTM architectures, generally outperform traditional models but require large training datasets and raise concerns related to interpretability and ethics. In terms of validation, hydro-climatic indices such as SPI and SPEI are most commonly used (32%), followed by crop yield and yield anomaly data (19%). This review further identifies key research gaps across sensors, indices, and modelling approaches and proposes a roadmap for developing equitable, interpretable, and resilient agricultural drought monitoring systems. Emerging opportunities include context-aware and interpretable AI, multi-sensor and multi-scale data fusion across optical, thermal, and microwave domains, integration of physiologically meaningful indicators such as sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), robust uncertainty quantification, and the development of hybrid and physics-informed modelling frameworks.

papers.title: An innovative approach of Project-based learning Applied to the teaching of biochemistry
papers.abstract: Most of the research in biochemistry education describes approaches that include teaching with constructivist ideas, since the approach with lectures has been criticized for promoting superficial learning. Thus, biochemistry learning should not only achieve proficiency of knowledge but also critical thinking skills and the interconnection of knowledges. Although Case-Based Learning is the most frequent methodology, Project-Based Active Learning, using individual and collective strengths, has received attention in recent years. With the aim of encouraging learning through doing, experimenting, problem-solving, teamwork, developing social skills, understanding, collaboration, partnership, and responsibility, the activity "Projeto de Divulgação Científica" has been implemented in the Integrated Biochemistry course of different undergraduate programs at Universidade Federal de São Paulo, since the pandemic. The students divide themselves into groups and the development of skills such as selection of bibliography, collaboration, communication, contextualization are their responsibility since the students are free to choose the project theme and conduct. In 2023 the overall failure rate in the course was 10% lower when compared to 2018 rates, before the project’s implementation. Additionally, a shift was observed over the years in the diversity of presentation formats. Initially, 28 out of 50 presentations were in pamphlet form. Recently, there has been a significant increase in the use of Instagram and videos, including TikTok, probably due to this generation's greater interest in social media. It can be concluded that both active student participation in the Projeto de Divulgação Científica activity and the increase in the number of extensionist students in the Instagram Project reflect the acceptance of this activity by undergraduate students as a form of learning and scientific literacy development. Furthermore, this approach has increased students' interest in biochemistry and scientific outreach, as indicated by the growing number of followers of the Scientific Outreach page (@bioquimatch_unifesp). This methodology has contributed to more effectively integrating students into the discipline and covering all topics discussed throughout the semester, thereby fostering increased interest among both students and the general population in science.

papers.abstract: Literacy and numeracy are essential competencies for enabling learners to understand information, solve problems, and apply knowledge in daily life. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of LENTERA AKSARA (Literacy and Numeracy for Real Action) in improving the competencies of learners at PKBM AL FATTAH, Tasikmalaya Regency. A quantitative approach was employed involving 50 learners, with competency measured through pretest and posttest assessments. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, normalized gain (N-Gain), normality and homogeneity tests, and hypothesis testing. These findings indicate that LENTERA AKSARA is effective in strengthening learners’ literacy and numeracy competencies through meaningful, contextual, and active learning experiences.

papers.title: Arthroscopic Reduction and Fixation of Impacted Humeral Head Reverse Hill‐Sachs Fracture With Absorbable Anchors for Acute Traumatic Posterior Shoulder Dislocation
papers.abstract: Abstract A minimally invasive technique is presented for the treatment of acute traumatic posterior shoulder dislocation with a reverse Hill‐Sachs lesion. Arthroscopic reduction was combined with internal fixation using 1 absorbable anchor. Under high‐definition arthroscopic visualization, precise anatomical reduction of the impacted anteromedial humeral head compression fracture was achieved. Absorbable anchors were inserted into the subchondral bone defect beneath the reduced fragment. Initial stability was provided, and congruity of the articular surface is maintained. Compared with conventional approaches, several advantages were shown. First, anatomical restoration and functional preservation were achieved. The osseous morphology of the humeral head was restored, and the subscapularis tendon was preserved. Postoperative recovery of shoulder function, particularly internal rotation, was facilitated. Second, minimal invasiveness and biocompatibility were emphasized. Tissue trauma was reduced, and visualization was improved. Mechanical support was provided during early healing, followed by gradual degradation of the implants and progressive load transfer to newly formed bone. Long‐term risks associated with metallic implants were avoided, including secondary removal and stress shielding. Finally, concomitant injuries could be managed concurrently under arthroscopic guidance.

papers.title: Recombinant BibA Protein from Streptococcus agalactiae as an Experimental Model for Teaching Biochemistry and Microbiology in the Context of Real Lab Day
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION The BibA protein (Group B Streptococcus Immunogenic Bacterial Adhesin) is an important virulence factor of Streptococcus agalactiae, involved in adhesion to epithelial cells and interaction with the complement regulatory protein C4-binding protein, promoting immune evasion. This surface protein is highly immunogenic and has been investigated as a potential target for vaccine development and diagnostic approaches. In addition to its clinical relevance, BibA can also be used as a didactic model to demonstrate fundamental concepts of microbiology, immunology, and biochemistry in experimental teaching activities. BibA contains an α-helical domain in the N-terminal region, a proline-rich region, and the LPXTG motif at the C-terminal end, responsible for anchoring the protein to the bacterial cell wall. In silico analyses indicate that the BibA fragment (34–622 aa), derived from serotype V and with an approximate molecular weight of 65 kDa, is conserved among major clinical serotypes. OBJECTIVES Previous studies from our research group showed that undergraduate students still present misconceptions about S. agalactiae. In addition, traditional microbiology laboratory practices are not always aligned with current challenges, such as the development of vaccines and new therapeutic strategies. METHODS STRATEGY Considering this context, Real Lab Day (RLD), an inquiry-based teaching initiative associated with the #Adote Project, was developed to bring students closer to scientific practice. The aim of this study was to implement an investigative teaching strategy using BibA as an experimental model and to evaluate student engagement in microbiology research. RESULTS Students participated in laboratory activities involving BibA purification and protein analysis by SDS-PAGE and Western blotting, followed by presentation of their results. Post-activity questionnaires showed that all participants rated their interest in microbiology research as good or excellent, highlighting the potential of this initiative as an active learning strategy. CONCLUSION Real Lab Day strategy effectively integrated theory and practice, increasing student engagement in microbiology research and promoting active, inquiry-based learning.

papers.title: Multi-Time-Scale Power and Energy Balance Optimization Method for Power Systems Considering Hydrogen Energy Storage Failures Under Dynamic Carbon Quota Allocation
papers.abstract: High renewable energy penetration significantly increases source-side uncertainty and makes power and energy balancing more difficult under carbon emission constraints. To improve the multi-time-scale power and energy balance of highly uncertain power systems, this paper proposes a low-carbon coordinated optimization method considering wind–photovoltaic output uncertainty, hydrogen energy storage availability uncertainty, and carbon quota constraints. Wind and photovoltaic uncertainty is described by joint scenarios, while the available capacities of electrolyzers and hydrogen fuel cells are characterized using Markov-chain-based capacity coefficients. On this basis, a multi-time-scale power and energy balance optimization framework is established by combining medium- and long-term stochastic energy task decomposition, day-ahead two-stage stochastic optimization, and intra-day model predictive control rolling correction. The medium- and long-term layer coordinates energy tasks and carbon budgets, the day-ahead layer forms a baseline power and energy balance plan, and the intra-day layer corrects real-time power deviations. In addition, a dynamic carbon quota mechanism related to load level, renewable energy penetration, and hydrogen energy storage system availability is introduced to reflect the impact of operating conditions on low-carbon scheduling. Case-study results show that the proposed method can maintain power and energy balance under renewable fluctuations and hydrogen energy storage availability variations. Compared with a static carbon quota scheme, the dynamic carbon quota mechanism reduces total operating cost by 8.94% and carbon emissions by 8.77%. The intra-day rolling correction reduces the RMSE of residual power deviations to 9.39 kW, indicating that the proposed optimization method can improve multi-time-scale balancing robustness and low-carbon operation capability of highly uncertain power systems.

papers.title: Beyond Memorization: A Puzzle-Based Approach to Deciphering the Glycolytic Pathway
papers.abstract: Biochemistry stands as a cornerstone within the biological and health sciences. However, its pedagogy often poses significant challenges for students, attributed mainly to the subject's abstract nature. This situation fosters a reliance on rote memorization, overshadowing conceptual understanding. There exists a pressing need for innovative pedagogical strategies that elevate learning beyond traditional paradigms, fostering more meaningful engagement. Evaluate the significant learning response in biochemistry teaching, through a ludic approach. The initiative seeks to demystify biochemical processes within the glycolytic pathway, thus enhancing learning and reducing dependence on memorization. In a higher education health sciences course, this study introduced an innovative pedagogical methodology in the field of biochemistry with a specific focus on the glycolytic pathway. A collaborative puzzle exercise was developed, in which the pieces represented compounds of the glycolytic pathway, provided in random order, with glucose and pyruvate identified. Students were tasked with arranging the compounds logically, observing structural changes, without external resources and without prior exposure to the correct sequence. Remarkably, all groups were able to correctly identify almost the entire sequence of the glycolytic pathway compounds to the correct sequence. This outcome not only underscores the effectiveness of the pedagogical approach in enhancing students' understanding and retention of complex biochemical concepts but also highlights the students' ability to apply logical reasoning and deductive skills in a constrained environment. Introducing ludic and collaborative tools, such as the glycolytic pathway puzzle, proved to be an effective strategy in transforming students' perceptions and learning experiences in biochemistry. By converting the subject from an abstract and challenging topic into a domain rich with logical patterns and active learning opportunities, this methodology holds potential for broader application across biochemistry education, promising widespread positive impacts on science education.

papers.title: ANALOG AND DIGITAL GAMES AS METHODOLOGICAL RESOURCES IN HISTORY TEACHING
papers.abstract: The use of analog and digital games in history teaching raises questions about student interest, historical learning, and teacher mediation. This article presents findings from the master’s study “Games and Digital Games versus Active Learning Methodologies: The Score in Historical Learning,” conducted within the Professional Graduate Program in History Teaching at the Federal University of Mato Grosso (UFMT), Brazil. It examines the possibilities and limitations of these resources in two sixth-grade classes, considering students’ perceptions of interest and learning and the role of teacher mediation. The qualitative study involved forty students at a state school in Alto Garças, Mato Grosso, combining participant observation, classroom records, learning assessments, questionnaires, and group discussions. One class participated in analog and digital game activities, including the board game “Exploring Prehistory: Tracing the Ways of Life of the Earliest Humans,” designed by the teacher-researcher, while the other engaged in Peer Instruction activities. Findings indicate that games fostered motivation and engagement, whereas Peer Instruction encouraged collaboration and knowledge sharing. Combining resources and teaching methods contributed to understanding historical content, although students perceived their contributions differently. The study concludes that the teacher’s methodological approach and mediation are essential to aligning these resources with teaching objectives and students’ needs, guiding their use toward a critical and reflective understanding of history.

papers.title: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Ni-Cr Alloy Coatings Processed via High-Velocity Oxygen-Fuel Spraying
papers.abstract: In this work, soft magnetic coatings were fabricated from Fe-Ni-Cr (1J38) alloy powders via high-velocity oxygen-fuel (HVOF) spraying. The microstructural features and intrinsic magnetic properties were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and a background signal stripping algorithm. Furthermore, the microstructural defects and magnetic degradation characteristics of coatings with varying thicknesses were comparatively analyzed. The results indicate that while the HVOF deposits exhibit exceptional density, the rapid quenching process inevitably induces oxygen-rich inter-splat boundary networks and residual stresses within the coatings. XRD analysis reveals no significant macroscopic oxidation or phase transformation during deposition, demonstrating a high-fidelity retention of the original face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice structure of the feedstock alloy. Magnetic measurements, upon the precise elimination of substrate background interference, reveal a distinct wasp-waisted magnetization distortion at low magnetic fields. This phenomenon can be attributed to the asynchronous magnetization response between the easily reversed, unoxidized soft-magnetic splat cores and the high-barrier boundary pinning networks (composed of inter-splat oxide interlayers and localized high-stress concentrations) within the coating. Compared to the thicker deposits (0.5 mm), the thinner coatings (0.3 mm) exhibit superior magnetic performance, characterized by a lower intrinsic coercivity. This degradation in thicker coatings is ascribed to the substantial accumulation of macroscopic residual stresses during deposition, which exert a stronger pinning effect on magnetic domain wall motion.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Driven Simulations of Hyperthermal Atomic Oxygen Impacts on (0001) Al2O3 for Low-Altitude Satellite Design.
papers.abstract: In Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO), spacecraft encounter residual atmosphere primarily composed of atomic oxygen (AO). The drag and operational lifetime of these spacecraft are determined by the interaction between AO and the surface, which for aluminum is a passivation layer of Al2O3. We present a blueprint for developing machine-learned interatomic potentials for reactive gas-surface systems. Gaussian-Moment Neural Networks, implemented in apax, are trained using an active learning workflow that incorporates a spin-state switching scheme. This approach accounts for the triplet-to-singlet transition that AO undergoes upon adsorption, a process usually neglected in machine-learned potential studies. This methodology enables the simulation of thousands of hyperthermal impacts on (0001) Al2O3 at orbital velocity with near-first-principles accuracy for systems four times larger and four orders of magnitude cheaper than ab initio molecular dynamics. Alumina is not an inert surface. Most impacting atoms adsorb rather than reflect, and with continuous exposure, the surface reaches a dynamic steady state where ∼14% of the binding sites are occupied. The surface remains intact. Atoms desorb primarily as O2 formed by recombination, indicating that surface chemistry, rather than simple scattering, governs the energy transfer during impact. Conventional spacecraft drag models assume that impacting atoms desorb thermally in equilibrium with the surface. Our findings demonstrate that this assumption is invalid for alumina. We determine an energy accommodation coefficient of 0.61, which is lower than the 0.82 to 1.0 range measured on actual spacecraft surfaces. This discrepancy quantifies the effect of technical surface roughness. When scaling the simulated momentum transfer to the European Space Agency's GOCE satellite, the measured reentry drag force is reproduced within a factor of 1.8. Since an atomically smooth surface still exhibits strong energy accommodation through chemical bond formation, effective drag reduction in VLEO requires materials that are both atomically smooth and chemically inert.
