papers.title: Power Prediction Method for High-Pressure Roll Mill Based on Long Short-Term Memory and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (LSTM-PINN)
papers.abstract: The accurate prediction of the power of high-pressure roller mills is considered essential for evaluating equipment operating conditions and optimizing energy consumption. Existing power prediction methods, however, are considered to have notable limitations: mechanistic models exhibit limited adaptability under dynamic conditions, and purely data-driven models lack physical logic constraints, often resulting in physically inconsistent predictions during extreme conditions such as shutdowns. To address these problems, proposed in this paper is a power prediction method that combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) under a sliding-window rolling prediction framework, termed LSTM-PINN. This method takes HPGR as the research object and integrates the LSTM-PINN framework with the physical mechanism of high-pressure roller mills for power prediction. Specifically, based on the physical operating mechanism of HPGR, four constraint relationships-monotonicity, linear prior, thermodynamic, and energy conservation-are introduced and embedded into the loss function of LSTM-PINN. While LSTM-PINN has been applied in other domains, its combination with the HPGR physical mechanism for power prediction has not been previously reported. The LSTM network extracts dynamic temporal features of power evolution, while the four mechanism-driven physical constraints guide the model toward physically consistent predictions. Experiments using actual operational data from a mining company demonstrate that: (1) the pure LSTM model outputs non-zero power during shutdown, whereas LSTM-PINN brings predictions to zero; (2) compared with pure LSTM, LSTM-PINN reduces RMSE by 23.13%, 13.02%, and 11.86%, and reduces MAE by 21.67%, 13.70%, and 10.85% under the single-feature, multi-feature, and all-feature input combinations, respectively. Among all configurations, the multi-feature combination achieves the lowest absolute errors with the smallest variance, representing the optimal trade-off between accuracy and stability. Overall, the proposed method substantially improves prediction accuracy, interpretability, and reliability, providing a trustworthy basis for energy optimization and intelligent control of HPGRs.

papers.title: DA PEDAGOGIA INCLUSIVA À EMPREGABILIDADE: Revisão sistemática sobre metodologias ativas, permanência acadêmica e transição escola–trabalho de estudantes com deficiência
papers.abstract: Este estudo analisa como práticas de educação inclusiva associadas a metodologias ativas contribuem para a permanência acadêmica e para a empregabilidade de estudantes com deficiência. Partiu-se da constatação de que a literatura tende a examinar separadamente práticas pedagógicas inclusivas, permanência institucional e inserção profissional, havendo escassez de investigações que integrem essas dimensões ao longo da trajetória formativa. Adotou-se revisão sistemática orientada pelo protocolo PRISMA 2020, com busca realizada na base Scopus por meio das strings “inclusive education” AND “active learning” e “students with disabilities” AND employability. Após identificação de 40 registros, remoção de duplicidades e aplicação dos critérios de inclusão e exclusão, 11 estudos compuseram o corpus final. Foi construída matriz de codificação analítica contemplando cinco eixos: identificação do estudo, dimensão pedagógica, permanência, transição laboral e resultados quantitativos. Os achados indicam que metodologias ativas associadas a adaptações curriculares e suporte institucional favorecem engajamento e desempenho acadêmico; que a permanência está relacionada à presença de tecnologias assistivas e formação docente consistente; e que programas estruturados de transição escola–trabalho apresentam taxas superiores a 60% de inserção competitiva. Conclui-se que inclusão educacional e inclusão produtiva constituem dimensões interdependentes de uma trajetória formativa contínua. O estudo propõe modelo conceitual integrativo que articula práticas pedagógicas, permanência e empregabilidade, oferecendo base empírica sistematizada para formulação de políticas públicas orientadas à sustentabilidade das trajetórias educacionais e profissionais.

papers.title: Gamification and case study for active learning of Chemistry in regular High School and Adult Education (EJA)
papers.abstract: In the technology era, the challenge in classrooms to achieve student engagement in chemistry teaching is growing every day. Active methodologies integrated with Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) have been studied and improved, allowing for the stimulation of student autonomy and participation. Recent studies reveal that gamification has yielded significant results in learning aligned with relevant theoretical frameworks. To qualitatively assess significant learning response in high school and EJA chemistry teaching through active methodologies. The gamification approach in high school, focusing on chemical equilibrium content, was implemented using a quiz on the KAHOOT platform. In Adult Education, the active methodology employed was a case study on organic functions content, involving the demonstration of physical-chemical parameter analysis experiments on regional water. Investigation of pedagogical practices exploring challenges and potentials of Active Methodologies was conducted. Qualitative data were collected through observation, questionnaires, experiments, and interviews. Through statistical data collection, analysis of focus group results, and observation of gamification activities in high school and case studies in EJA, we discussed the effectiveness of these approaches in chemistry teaching. Strategies that elicited student interest, promoted active participation, and facilitated content comprehension were identified, providing insights to enhance pedagogical practices. KAHOOT quiz results showed varied performance among classes, highlighting the utility of gamification. Case study results in EJA revealed a positive impact of activities on inorganic functions, promoting deep understanding and awareness of the importance of water treatment. By incorporating gamification and case studies into chemistry teaching, we observed positive results, with students demonstrating interest in learning due to the differentiated approach, facilitating the learning process, and making it more enjoyable and spontaneous. These findings confirm that these methodologies fostered greater interaction among students during chemistry teaching.

papers.title: On Porosity Analysis of Ti-6Al-4V Thin Struts Made by Laser Powder-Bed Fusion: Effects of Build Orientation, Strut Size and Linear Energy Density
papers.abstract: Porosity in laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) lattice struts remains poorly understood, as the effects of build angle and process parameters are often studied separately. A full factorial design of 27 configurations combined three build angles (40–70°), three strut sizes (0.25–1.25 mm), and three linear energy densities (LED: 0.23–0.35 J/mm). Specimens were fabricated in Ti-6Al-4V on an EOS M270 system and characterized by micro-computed tomography (µ-CT). Statistical analysis showed that all three factors influenced porosity percentage (P%), with a significant size–LED interaction, while only strut size and LED influenced the average volume of individual pores (PVavg), with no significant interactions. P% rose 194% as strut diameter increased from 0.25 to 1.25 mm, climbed steeply between 0.23 and 0.29 J/mm before plateauing, and fell 19% as build angle increased from 40° to 70°. PVavg rose 160% across the LED range and 37% with strut diameter. Spatial segmentation showed that the median down-skin-to-up-skin pore volume ratio in the larger struts fell from 2.0 at 40°, that is, twice the pore volume in the DS region, to 1.3 at 70°. This asymmetry was absent in the 0.25 mm struts, where low pore counts made the metric unreliable.

papers.title: Development and validation of a nomogram for predicting the probability of arthroplasty in patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head after fibular strut grafting
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: While fibular strut grafting (FSG) is effective for osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH), some patients still progress to total hip arthroplasty (THA). This study aimed to identify risk factors for FSG failure and develop a validated nomogram to predict the mid-long term survival rate after FSG. METHODS: Data on patients with ONFH who underwent FSG were collected in our institution from February 2009 to December 2018. Independent predictors were identified using univariable and multivariable Cox regression analyses. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate survival after FSG. A nomogram predicting failure, defined as conversion to THA, was developed from the selected predictors and internally validated using the concordance index (C index), the Receiver Operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and calibration curves. RESULTS: Among 416 eligible patients, 55 converted to THA. The 5-, 8-, and 10-year survival rates after FSG were 89.7%, 83.6%, and 82%, respectively. Age, smoking, Fibrinogen (FIB), hypertension, diabetes, and ARCO stage were independent predictors of failure. Subsequently, a nomogram model was developed incorporating 7 predictors (including JIC classification). Its C-index was 0.734 (95%CI 0.66-0.80). The area under the curves (AUCs) of the nomogram predicted for 5-, 8-, and 10-year were 0.727, 0.735, and 0.735, respectively. Predicted and observed survival rates agreed closely. CONCLUSION: The internal validation shows that the nomogram model has acceptable discriminative ability and good accuracy. It may support clinical application, effectively optimize perioperative management, and help doctors and patients to avoid FSG failure.
